title: Deep Learning Classification of Canine Behavior Using a Single Collar-Mounted Accelerometer: Real-World Validation.
summary: The MDPI article and the linked first bioRxiv version (2020-12-14) both report deep-learning classification of dog behavior from collar accelerometers together with real-world owner validation; the preprint abstract reports more than 5,000 videos from 2,500 dogs, more than 11 million device-days, and 10,550 dogs with 163,110 event responses, with eating and drinking sensitivity and specificity and in-production true-positive rates. The two versions agree on these claims. External replication and prospective utility were not established.
ai_technology: Learned behavior classifier received real-world user validation at scale; labels are owner reports and validation covers mainly eating/drinking, not every behavior.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Primary MDPI article plus linked bioRxiv v1 (2020-12-14) confirm deep-learning collar accelerometer behavior classification and real-world owner validation; v1 abstract reports >5,000 videos/2,500 dogs, >11 million device-days, 10,550 dogs/163,110 event responses, eating/drinking sensitivity/specificity and production true-positive rates. Full v1 HTML was accessed; core result-bearing claims agree with journal article.
evidence.unknown: External replication, causal effects and prospective utility were not established in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Learned behavior classifier received real-world user validation at scale; labels are owner reports and validation covers mainly eating/drinking, not every behavior.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
